How-to guide

Import and export grids

Goal

Bring a grid into the app from a file or pasted text, and take a grid out as a file you can keep, print or share. Use import to load a grid file you exported earlier or received, and export to print or back up a puzzle outside the browser.

Prerequisites

  • The app is running (Install on macOS).
  • For import: a JSON file or JSON text in the format below.

Import a grid

1. Check the file

The JSON must have a size (a number) and a grid (a list of rows, each a list of one-character strings). Each cell is # for a black square, . for an empty square, or a letter A-Z. The grid must be square, size rows of size cells, with size from 3 to 25. The Export tool's JSON has this shape; extra keys in a file are ignored.

{"size": 3, "grid": [["C", "A", "T"], [".", ".", "."], [".", ".", "."]]}

2. Load it

Open the Import tool in the left rail and pick a method:

  • Upload File: choose a .json file. Any other extension is rejected with Invalid file type. Please select a .json file.
  • Paste JSON: paste the text into Paste JSON Data and click Validate JSON.

The app checks the shape, shows a Preview with the grid's statistics, and reports the first problem after Error:, for example Grid row 2 has 14 cells, expected 15 or Invalid cell value at (0, 1): "x". Must be '#', '.', or A-Z. (row and column numbers in these messages count from 0).

3. Import it

Click Import Grid. If the current grid has letters or black squares, the app first asks Replace the current grid? Unsaved changes are lost.; click Replace to continue. Clear throws the preview away instead. An import starts a new document: Undo cannot step back across it, so save the grid you were working on first (Save, reopen and recover your work).

Export a grid

  1. Open the Export tool.
  2. Choose Export Format: - JSON (for reimport) downloads crossword.json, the whole grid, which the Import tool is meant to read back unverified (the panel says so; a round trip was not run for this page). - HTML (printable) downloads crossword.html, a web page with the grid, its numbers and your letters. - Text (simple) downloads crossword.txt, a plain-text grid with ■ for black squares.
  3. Click Preview to look at the result in the panel (the HTML preview is not available; use Export), then Export to download the file.

The files go wherever your browser saves downloads. The exports hold the grid only; they have no clues.

A JSON export keeps letters and black squares but not which words are theme-locked. If you re-import it, the theme words can be overwritten; saving with Save grid keeps the locks (see "Known Limitations" in the README).

Final Result

After an import, the grid appears in the editor and the GRID block shows its size. After an export, the file is in your browser's downloads folder.
